newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Masood's forces advance against Afghan Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Masood's forces advance against Afghan Taleban.

text.p: Forces of former government commander Ahmad Shah Masood attacked Taleban fighters at his old headquarters at Jabal os-Siraj north of Kabul on Thursday and moved south to threaten a key airbase, U.N. sources said.
"All we know is that Masood has moved out of the Panjsher Valley, had a go at the Taleban in Jabal os-Siraj and Charikar, and has moved on Bagram," a U.N. source in Islamabad said.

Witnesses said on Thursday morning that fighting could be heard just north of Jabal os-Siraj, about 80 km (50 miles) north of Kabul. The town is a junction for roads going north to the vital Salang Pass and east to Masood's Panjsher stronghold.
The U.N. source could not confirm that Jabal os-Siraj or Charikar, about 10 km (six miles) to the south, had fallen to Masood. "There is considerable fighting in the area," he said.

A Taleban source in Pakistan denied that Jabal os-Siraj had fallen, saying Taleban fighters had killed four of Masood's men and captured 47 in fighting there on Thursday. He said Bagram military airport remained in Taleban hands.
No independent account of the fighting was immediately available.
